newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures fall sharply on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures fall sharply on profit taking.

text.p: CME lumber futures fell for sharp losses as profit taking offset early demand from strong cash, traders said.
November fell for a sharp loss of $8.40 per tbf and at 0929 CDT stood $8.00 lower at $398.00 per tbf. Other months were off $8.30 to $1.80.

Carryover demand linked to a recent sharp rise in cash lumber prices pushed lumber futures higher, floor sources said. But profit taking quickly weighed on prices, especially after the sharp price gains this week and posting of new contract highs in November and January Thursday, they said.
Some correction of the November/January spread also weighed on November, they said.
Much of the cash strength this week was already in the market but further advances in cash will provide underlying support, they added.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $405 per tbf, up $17 from midweek and $27 above last Friday's quote. Gains came on strong consumption and speculation some Canadian mills have already met their annual quota of free export allotments.
Cash sources noted that cash lumber prices are more in the $415 to $420 per tbf area.
